questions.q: 2,3-Dimethylbut-2-ene is treated with cold, dilute, alkaline KMnO₄ (Baeyer's reagent). The product is:
questions.explain: Baeyer's reagent forms a cyclic manganate ester that is hydrolysed to the vicinal diol, both OH groups added to the same face (syn). Cleavage to propanone needs hot or acidified KMnO₄.

questions.q: Which alkylbenzene does NOT give benzoic acid on heating with KMnO₄?
questions.explain: Side-chain oxidation needs at least one hydrogen on the benzylic carbon. In tert-butylbenzene that carbon carries three methyl groups and no H; every other chain is cut back to a single COOH.

questions.q: In neutral or weakly alkaline solution, permanganate acts as an oxidant by accepting three electrons. It is reduced to:
questions.explain: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻. Mn²⁺ forms in acid (5e⁻) and green manganate MnO₄²⁻ in strongly alkaline solution (1e⁻).

questions.q: Butan-2-one is heated with KMnO₄. According to Popoff's rule, the product is:
questions.explain: The C=O stays with the smaller alkyl group, so the bond on the ethyl side breaks: CH₃CO– becomes ethanoic acid and the ethyl CH₂ is oxidised to a second ethanoic acid.
